component.name: BananaSplit
component.summary: Virtual audio mixer with cables, buses and a recorder

description.p: BananaSplit mixes, routes and records audio on PipeWire: 6 strips and 5 buses with EQ, virtual cables to send any app's sound where you want it, VBAN over the network and a recorder that writes MP3 or WAV.
It lives in the tray, and closing its window keeps the mixer running.
macOS: only the user BananaSplit runs as can control it, and a device whose sample format changes is opened again. Nothing changes on Linux and Windows.
BananaSplit now also comes as an app for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), on Core Audio with BlackHole as virtual cables. Nothing changes on Linux.

The last part of the Rust code review: every unsafe block explains why it is sound, the code is lint-clean and checked on every change, and all calls into C and Windows libraries are declared in one place per platform.

More under-the-hood hardening from the Rust code review: the code that talks to JACK, the tray and Windows audio is harder to misuse, and a Windows audio thread that cannot start no longer leaves devices open.
Under-the-hood fixes from a Rust code review: tray and dark-style checks no longer leak memory or trip on unexpected replies, and recording moves less data between threads.
A silent take is shown only by the recorder's orange "Recording silence" label; the long notice below the recorder is gone.
An app ticked in a strip's menu keeps that strip after a restart, also apps that don't choose their own device (such as Strawberry); the list of apps and strips can be edited by hand.
Recordings go into a folder per day; a take that runs past midnight continues in the next day's folder, and the player still lists it as one take.

Apps go back to their strip when BananaSplit starts again, so a recording no longer stays silent after an update; the recorder warns when a take records only silence; the open window needs far less CPU.
Fixes from the 2.8.2 review: the window no longer opens empty on virtual machines, software rendering or hybrid laptops, and the recording state lists only the files being written.
BananaSplit is available as a Flatpak.
